chain.title: Bring the Bees Home Safely
chain.desc: Make Bee Cages before exploring. Capture a bee with a cage and release it near suitable housing and its required flower or food source.

chain.title: A Treat for New Neighbors
chain.desc: Prepare Honey Treats. They are used in several bee workflows, including repopulating an empty nest and helping young bees grow.

chain.title: Find the Right Nest
chain.desc: Configure the Nest Locator against the nest type you want, then search nearby. Different wild bees use different nests and habitats.

chain.title: A Hive for Resource Bees
chain.desc: Build an Advanced Beehive and move suitable productive bees into it. Solitary nest bees and hive bees do not all use the same housing.

chain.title: Put the Right Food Within Reach
chain.desc: Prepare the Feeding Slab and supply the exact flowering material the bee needs. Check the bee's recipe-viewer page; ordinary flowers do not satisfy every species.

chain.title: The First Productive Hive
chain.desc: House a compatible bee, provide its correct flowering material, and collect its resource combs after a completed trip. Confirm when the hive actually produces.

chain.title: Separate the Resource Combs
chain.desc: Process the combs in a Centrifuge to recover their resources and honey. Provide output space and remove fluid before the machine backs up.

chain.title: Room for More Bees and Upgrades
chain.desc: Attach a matching Expansion Box to the Advanced Hive. The expanded hive gains more bee capacity and enables its upgrade slots.

chain.title: Choose How the Hive Improves
chain.desc: Craft an Upgrade Base for specialized upgrades. Choose productivity, simulation or another real need instead of installing upgrades without supporting supplies.

chain.title: More from Each Trip
chain.desc: Install a Productivity Upgrade in an eligible expanded hive. Verify that its comb output increases over several production cycles.

chain.title: Keep Production Inside the Hive
chain.desc: Install a Simulation Upgrade and put the bee's required flowering block or feeding slab in the documented position at the foot of the hive. Bees now simulate their trips inside.

chain.title: Help the Next Generation Grow
chain.desc: Put a caged baby bee and Honey Treats in the Incubator. The machine also supports the bee-type gene and egg workflow described in the guide.

chain.title: Breed with a Plan
chain.desc: Build a Breeding Chamber and supply the two required parent bees, breeding foods, power and empty cages. The parents' species determine the possible offspring.

chain.title: Keep Up with More Hives
chain.desc: Upgrade to a Powered Centrifuge and provide FE. Increase item and fluid output capacity alongside machine speed.

chain.title: Organize the Genetics Work
chain.desc: Build a Gene Indexer for the genetics branch. Collect and process the correct bee material before organizing or applying genes.

chain.title: Prove Your Breeding Result
chain.desc: Breed a useful new bee, grow it, and establish it in suitable housing with the correct flower. Confirm after the new bee produces the resource you planned.

chain.title: The Apiary Runs a Full Cycle
chain.desc: Connect hive comb output to processing and route both resources and honey to storage. Confirm after repeated cycles run without blocked outputs.

content_revision: 2026-10-07: explicit branches, operational guidance, no collection filler

coverage.scope: Bee capture and housing, real pollination, comb processing, breeding, genetics and simulated production.
coverage.limitations: Data and bundled English guide checked against 12.6.0. Configurable bees and combs require species data, so generic untyped comb items are not used as fake resource milestones.
coverage.verification_detail: Item models, entity language identifiers, dimension data, recipes and bundled guide text where present were inspected; this is data verification, not a Minecraft playthrough.

notes: Each requires list is intentional. Empty lists are independent entry routes. Links describe guided progression or demonstrated recipe/boss gates, not an assertion that every dependency is a game-enforced lock. Runtime scanning still filters unavailable items and entities.
